Area Forecast Discussion...UPDATED
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
916 PM EDT Fri Aug 7 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
All watches and warnings were dropped earlier. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...

- 1) Patchy morning fog, high humidity, hot temperatures, and 
  daily thunderstorm chances continue through early next week. 

- 2) A cold front could arrive late next week and into the 
  weekend bringing relief from the heat and humidity.

&&

.DISCUSSION...

KEY MESSAGE 1... Patchy morning fog, high humidity, hot 
temperatures, and daily thunderstorm chances continue through 
early next week. 

Somewhat similar conditions to what occurred today are expected
Saturday as another potent shortwave passes through. The main 
difference is that mid-level flow turns a bit more W to WSW 
versus the SW'ly flow we have had in recent days. As a result, 
coverage of storms is likely to be less than what we saw today.
However, shear values increase a bit, reaching 30 to 35 kts as 
the subtropical jet stream begins to strengthen. Mid- level 
lapse rates are also impressive, similar to today's event. 
Instability will be a bit less tomorrow, owing to the westerly 
mid-level flow. Thermodynamic profiles depict skinnier CAPE 
profiles, but inverted-V signatures towards the surface. Our 
thoughts are that the coverage should be less tomorrow, but the 
ceiling could be higher in terms of damaging wind potential, 
should storms be able to develop and get organized. The Storm 
Prediction Center has added a Marginal Risk for severe weather 
tomorrow as a result that encompasses much of the forecast area,
further reinforcing our thoughts. 

Convection begins to wane a bit Sunday into Monday given quasi-zonal 
flow aloft. A few storms may develop over the higher elevations,
but coverage will be much less than in recent days. This will 
be short-lived however, with storm chances increasing once 
again Tuesday through the end of the week as a series of 
shortwave disturbances pass through. 

Outside of the storm chances expect highs in the upper 80s and low 
90s with heat indices east of the Blue Ridge up around 100 
degrees. The hottest days look to be Sunday through Tuesday 
given the strengthened subtropical ridge over the region.


KEY MESSAGE 2...A cold front could arrive late next week and 
into the weekend bringing relief from the heat and humidity. 

While this is very far out in the forecast period, there is some 
signal that a more potent frontal system could push through the 
region late in the week. The details are murky at this stage of the 
forecast, with timing very uncertain, as well as potential impacts. 
Deterministic and ensemble guidance are generally between 
Thursday/Friday right now, with improvement in the weather 
pattern possible into the upcoming weekend. Any decent frontal 
passage in the summertime should be watched closely for 
potential severe weather, so we will keep monitoring this in the
coming days to see if that potential is there, and try to 
narrow down the timeframe a bit more.

&&

.AVIATION /01Z SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
Prevailing VFR conditions are expected across the terminals 
through the middle of next week given subtropical high pressure 
offshore and the lack of any real front passing through. Brief 
periods of sub-VFR are likely during the afternoon and evening 
hours due to thunderstorms, though Sunday and Monday look to
have the lowest chances, and primarily at MRB and CHO. 

More storms are expected Saturday afternoon and evening, but 
with less coverage. Added a 3 hour PROB30 for now, as the 
likelihood of storms tomorrow is less than today, and there is a
lot more uncertainty with convective initiation than we have 
today. As we get closer, will refine that forecast and add 
TEMPOs or FM groups as necessary. 

Outside of the thunderstorms expect patchy fog between the 
terminals each morning through early next week. Winds will 
remain light out of the south and southeast at less than 15 kts.

&&

.MARINE...
SCA is in effect for portions of the Chesapeake Bay today due to
southerly channeling. However, the bigger threat will be with
storms this afternoon/evening, which will likely necessitate
some SMWs. Damaging wind gusts and frequent cloud-to-ground
lightning will be the main threats. 

Small Craft Advisories may be needed again on Saturday due to 
southerly channeling mainly in the afternoon and evening.
Another chance for storms Saturday afternoon, which could again
bring damaging winds and frequent lightning. However, a bit more
uncertainty with tomorrow's event in terms of coverage. 

A break from showers and storms is expected on Sunday and Monday
with winds generally gusting 10-15 knots at most during the
afternoon/evening hours.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Tidal anomalies climb through the weekend in response to return 
southerly flow. Periods of coastal flooding are possible at times of 
high tide at sensitive locations.

&&

.LWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
DC...None.
MD...None.
VA...None.
WV...None.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory until 11 PM EDT this evening for ANZ534-
     537-543.

&&
